captions.linkedin:
Apartment buyers in Qatar may start asking a new question: who runs the building?

Qatar's Real Estate Regulatory Authority (Aqarat) is highlighting Law No. (11) of 2026 on Owners' Associations. According to a QNA report published by The Peninsula on 27 November, the law sets a framework for how owners of jointly-owned properties relate to each other, defines their rights and obligations, and encourages them to take part in decisions.

The aim: common areas and facilities managed efficiently, transparently and sustainably, protecting owners' interests and long-term investment value.

In Aqarat's words, the association "transforms the owner from a mere recipient of services into an active partner in managing the property."

Why it matters for agencies:
→ Buyers and investors in towers and shared communities will want to know how the building is run.
→ Well-managed common areas are a selling point. Treat them like one in listings and viewings.
→ Agents who understand the framework sound more credible than agents who guess.

What to do now:
Read Aqarat's official guidance, brief your team, and prepare a short, accurate answer for clients. Don't fill in details the law's text hasn't confirmed.
